farm_compass: In the answers, "north" means along the barn toward the wooden garage (bearing ~40°) and "west" means the barn's ramp side.

Farmhouse: Same place as today's house. Two storeys.
Porch on the west side with a door, but everyone used the south-facing front door.
Front door: up a few concrete steps covered in black outdoor carpet, railings on both sides. The door is slightly left of the middle of the steps, with a white metal bench to its right.

From the photo: white horizontal siding, slate-blue window trim, corner boards and roof edges, dark charcoal shingles, a buff brick chimney at the ridge, and a rounded fieldstone foundation like the barn's.
From the photo: a steep front gable with an octagonal vent near the peak, and a one-storey porch with white posts, white railings, a white lattice skirt and a gooseneck light by its door.
Wooden garage: Attached to the barn. Roof slants down toward the north.
Door faces west. Painted red to match the barn.
Large red barn: Same barn, same place as today. Rounded fieldstone foundation about 8 ft high.
Gable roof with its two slopes facing west and east, black shingles. A large green Christmas tree with a white star on top is painted on the west slope.
White trim across the whole barn and its doors.
Upper floor: two very large sliding doors at the top of the ramp, opening left and right, big enough for tractors.
Ground floor, south side: one giant sliding door with a normal-size walk-through door cut into it, and a basketball hoop (no net).
Ramp, well and sandbox: The ramp was paved. Everything else around it was gravel.
South of the ramp: a small open sandbox of plain wood with a blue plastic cover.
North of the ramp, before the garage: the remains of an old stone well, no longer used.
Gravel driveway: All open gravel, graded for driving and parking. No grass inside it.
Mailbox at the entrance. Nothing permanently parked.
The gravel outline on the map matches your memory.
Tall aluminum windmill: About 15 ft taller than the house.
Orchard: Lines run parallel with the length of the barn. About 10 trees per line, about 9 lines.
Grafted apple trees about 13 ft tall, branches trained so the apples hang about 5 ft up.
The 2 westernmost lines were a mix of pear and cherry trees.
Grape vines and garden: 4 rows. Shortened by 20% at the north end.
A small garden of vegetables and flowers, about 10 × 7 ft, in that space.
Red wooden garage: Door faces north. Black shingle roof.
Wire corn crib: Round wire-mesh corn crib, about 8 ft tall, half full of corn.
Red wooden shed: The circle you drew at its corner was the corn crib, so the shed sits right beside it.
Clear plexiglass greenhouse: Peaked roof. Aluminum frame and plexiglass.
Christmas tree rows: Scotch pine, Douglas fir, white pine and blue spruce, in bands from west to east.
Very orderly grid. Longer lines simply hold more trees.
Sizes random throughout (15% knee high, 50% about 6 ft, 35% 8 to 10 ft), because each cut tree was replaced by a baby the next year.
The X tree was nothing special, and the corner trees were just where the block ended.
Pumpkin patch: Fills the full width of the south end.
Past the south line: a rising hill of grass, wildflowers and weeds.
Old rusted barrel stove: A small pile of scrap wood next to it.
Clothes lines: Three lines, two sets of posts.
Kids' small playhouse: Black shingle roof, nothing on top.
Trees, paths and fields: The big tree was a very large Scotch pine.
The northeast row was evergreen spruce.
Dashed lines and the south lane were mowed grass paths, often with tractor tyre marks.
The blank land east of the barn was a field of weeds, grass and wildflowers.
The land as a whole: About 5 acres. Same property line as the red line today.
South slope: about 20 ft down to the pumpkin patch, slight on the north side and steeper toward the bottom.
West slope: about 15 ft down to the road corner. North of the house, the ground also falls toward the road.
The yard rises slightly as you drive toward the farmhouse.
The road was a paved country road with a lot of aged cracking.
No fences: natural borders of prairie and trees. Neighbouring farmhouses to the northeast and southwest, behind trees.
The season to capture: lush green summer into early fall, fruit on the trees, flowers blooming, sunshine.
